title: The Lord of the Rings (BBC Radio)
paragraphs: BBC Radio 4 adaptation of Tolkien’s novel.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Original 26-part BBC Radio 4 serial (March 8, 1981 to August 30, 1981) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]] and BBC 13-part hour edit (July 17, 1982 to October 9, 1982) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Brian Sibley (radio adaptor), Gerard Murphy (narrator), Ian Holm (performer), Jane Morgan (director), Michael Bakewell (radio adaptor), Penny Leicester (director), and Stephen Oliver (composer).
The stories often return to epic fantasy, quest and fellowship, the One Ring and burden of power, Middle-earth, war against Sauron, and BBC prestige literary adaptation.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Original 26-part BBC Radio 4 serial, Thirteen-part hour-long re-edit, Earlier BBC Lord of the Rings adaptation, and 2002 BBC reissue and rerun.

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Brian Sibley (radio adaptor), Gerard Murphy (narrator), Ian Holm (performer), Jane Morgan (director), Michael Bakewell (radio adaptor), Penny Leicester (director), and Stephen Oliver (composer).

The stories often return to epic fantasy, quest and fellowship, the One Ring and burden of power, Middle-earth, war against Sauron, and BBC prestige literary adaptation.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Original 26-part BBC Radio 4 serial, Thirteen-part hour-long re-edit, Earlier BBC Lord of the Rings adaptation, and 2002 BBC reissue and rerun.
